text:
Yara: quick heads-up — hit a nasty typing + runtime mismatch when using our JS SDK in an Edge demo. Default import of the factory loses overload inference after bundling; methods show up as `any`.

Ibrahim: Oof. Can you paste a minimal repro?

Yara: repro:
```ts
// app tsconfig: module=ESNext, moduleResolution=NodeNext
import Client from 'redwood-sdk';
const c = Client(); // expected typed client, ends up as any
c.request({}) // no overload unions or generics inferred
```

Pri: two separate problems often: 1) runtime import shape changes because bundler transforms default exports to namespace objects for CJS interop; 2) the published package's types and conditional exports don't align, so TS resolves a different entry than the runtime.

Gupta: do we publish types under the export conditions? If types are only at top-level `types` that can cause different resolution in NodeNext vs bundled consumers.

Yara: package.json looks like: "exports": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"}, "types":"dist/index.d.ts" — so yeah, TS may pick the d.ts but the bundler chooses mjs and rewrites imports.

Ibrahim: immediate consumer workaround: explicitly call with generics `Client<MySchema>()` or use `import * as SDK` and access the named factory if it exists. But both are rough.

Pri: longer-term SDK fixes we should do: add a stable named export `export function createClient<T = any>(opts?: ...)` and keep `export default createClient` for compatibility. Also publish per-condition types in `exports` so `import` condition points to a `.d.mts` or types entry. Eg:
```json
"exports": {
  "import": {"types":"./dist/index.d.mts","default":"./dist/index.mjs"},
  "require": {"types":"./dist/index.d.cts","default":"./dist/index.cjs"}
}
```
That makes TS+runtime pick the same shape.

Gupta: +1. Also consider adding a `typesVersions` mapping for NodeNext consumers and emitting both ESM and CJS dts bundles (`index.d.mts` / `index.d.cts`) so TS can resolve correctly.

Yara: another friction: someone flipped a default generic from `any` to `unknown` in a minor patch and a bunch of callers started failing. We need guidance: which default should the SDK use?

Ibrahim: ergonomics matter. Keep `any` as default generic to avoid breaking consumer code. If teams want stricter typing, provide `createStrictClient<T>()` or a `StrictClient` wrapper type that uses `unknown`/narrower constraints. Changing the default generic is semver-major.

Pri: extra checks: add a release-time smoke that packs the current build (`npm pack`) and installs it into a small sample edge app, then run the actual production esbuild pipeline and TypeScript check. Fail the release if types vs runtime shape disagree.

Gupta: also add a lint rule in our monorepo release job to flag packages that only export a default factory without a named counterpart. Prevents regressions.

Yara: filed issue #5132 with repro and a tiny sample. For consumers until we ship fixes: 1) prefer named import (when available), 2) pass explicit generics, or 3) switch tsconfig to `moduleResolution: "Bundler"` in some cases — that helped in experiments but isn't a universal fix.

ci-bot: queued CI run "edge-sdk-typing-smoke" for branch fix/5132 — will build + pack + typecheck the sample.

Ibrahim: I'll open the named-export PR and add the per-condition types change. Also adding docs to onboarding explaining `Bundler` vs `NodeNext` choices.

Pri: thanks all — keeping this thread open until CI passes and PR lands. Ping here when ready.
